decision.name: Cellfie · Conway's Game of Life, one generation

generation.desc: The generation on the board now, counted from 0

rules.desc: Which rules are enabled: conway, Conway's own rules (B3/S23: a cell is born with three live neighbours and survives with two or three); highlife, HighLife's extra birth (B6: a dead cell with six live neighbours is also born, which lets replicators grow); no_death, Life without death (a live cell never dies, so patterns only grow). A live cell no enabled rule keeps alive dies.

situations.desc: Every distinct situation on the board: whether the cell is alive, how many of its 8 neighbours are alive, and how many cells are in that situation. The rest of the infinite board, dead cells with no live neighbour, is left out: the rules keep it dead.
situations.from: the app's board, counted cell by cell

clusters.desc: Every group of live cells on the board (cells within two of each other), with how many cells it has, its width and height, and its shape: rows of o (alive) and . (dead) joined by /, in the one of its turned and flipped forms that sorts first, so a pattern reads the same whichever way it faces.
clusters.from: the app's board, grouped cell by cell

body: Life without death: a live cell never dies, whatever its neighbours.
HighLife: a dead cell with exactly six live neighbours is also born, which lets replicators grow.
Underpopulation: a live cell with fewer than two live neighbours dies.
Survival: a live cell with two or three live neighbours lives on to the next generation.
Overpopulation: a live cell with more than three live neighbours dies.
Reproduction: a dead cell with exactly three live neighbours becomes a live cell.
No enabled rule keeps the live cell alive: it dies.
A dead cell no enabled rule brings to life stays dead.

The acorn, a methuselah: seven cells that take 5,206 generations to grow to 633 cells, with 13 gliders escaping.
Not in the catalogue: a soup, a pattern mid-change, or one the catalogue doesn't know.

fates.desc: What happens to the cells in each situation, in the order the situations were sent
fates.expr: for s in situations return fate(s.alive, s.neighbours, rules.conway, rules.highlife, rules.no_death)

alive_next.desc: Whether the cells in each situation are alive in the next generation, in the same order
alive_next.expr: for f in fates return f = "survives" or f = "is_born"

population.expr: if count(situations) = 0 then 0 else sum(for s in situations return if s.alive then s.cells else 0)

population_next.desc: Cells alive in the next generation
population_next.expr: if count(situations) = 0 then 0 else sum(for i in 1..count(situations) return if alive_next[i] then situations[i].cells else 0)

births.desc: Cells born in the next generation
births.expr: if count(situations) = 0 then 0 else sum(for i in 1..count(situations) return if fates[i] = "is_born" then situations[i].cells else 0)

deaths.desc: Cells that die, of loneliness, crowding or no rule keeping them
deaths.expr: if count(situations) = 0 then 0 else sum(for i in 1..count(situations) return if fates[i] = "dies_lonely" or fates[i] = "dies_crowded" or fates[i] = "dies_no_rule" then situations[i].cells else 0)

survivors.expr: if count(situations) = 0 then 0 else sum(for i in 1..count(situations) return if fates[i] = "survives" then situations[i].cells else 0)

patterns.desc: What each cluster is, in the order the clusters were sent: a pattern of the catalogue, or unknown
patterns.expr: for c in clusters return identify(c.cells, c.width, c.height, c.shape)

kinds.desc: What kind of pattern each cluster is, in the same order
kinds.expr: for p in patterns return kind_of(p)

recognized.desc: How many clusters are patterns of the catalogue
recognized.expr: if count(clusters) = 0 then 0 else sum(for p in patterns return if p = "unknown" then 0 else 1)
